title: Threshold of linear thresholds
statement: Let $n$ and $s$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$. Suppose there are $s$ linear threshold functions $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ and a real constant $c$ such that, for every input $x$, the real value of $f(x)$ is $c+\sum_{i=1}^s g_i(x)$, where each sign is viewed as its real value. Then $f$ is a threshold of those $s$ linear threshold functions: there are real weights and a real threshold offset such that $f(x)$ is the sign of the resulting weighted sum of $g_i(x)$, with zero assigned sign $+1$.
hypotheses_covered: A representation of the real value of $f$ as a constant plus a sum of $s$ linear threshold functions
